Source passages:

[1] Source: NIST.SP.800-53r4.pdf | "NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4: Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations"
    Metadata: date=2013-04-30 | version=Rev 4 | status=withdrawn
Special Publication 800-53 Revision 4 2.2 SECURITY CONTROL STRUCTURE Security controls described in this publication have a well-defined organization and structure. For ease of use in the security control selection and specification process, controls are organized into eighteen families. Each family contains security controls related to the general security topic of the family. A two-character identifier uniquely identifies security control families, for example, PS (Personnel Security). Table 1 lists the security control families and the associated family identifiers in the security control catalog.     Metadata: date=2020-09-23 | version=Rev 5 | status=active

Each family contains controls that are related to the specific topic of the family. A two-character identifier uniquely identifies each control family (e.g., PS for Personnel Security).     Metadata: date=2020-09-23 | version=Rev 5 | status=active

2.2 SECURITY CONTROL STRUCTURE Security controls described in this publication have a well-defined organization and structure. Table 1 lists the security control families and the associated family identifiers in the security control catalog. Special Publication 800-53 Revision 4 2.2 SECURITY CONTROL STRUCTURE Security controls described in this publication have a well-defined organization and structure. For ease of use in the security control selection and specification process, controls are organized into eighteen families. Each family contains security controls related to the general security topic of the family. A two-character identifier uniquely identifies security control families, for example, PS (Personnel Security). Table 1 lists the security control families and the associated family identifiers in the security control catalog.
